ambiguities.text: The documentation only covers get_valid_jump_destinations() but does not document other runtime functions like message call processing or contract creation.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume other runtime functions follow standard EVM semantics as defined in the Yellow Paper and prior fork specifications.

ambiguities.text: The handling of 'invalid opcodes' during bytecode iteration is mentioned but not fully specified.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume invalid opcodes are treated as single-byte instructions for iteration purposes, not causing analysis failure.

ambiguities.text: The behavior when PUSH data extends beyond bytecode bounds is not explicitly defined.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume PUSH instructions at the end of bytecode that would reference out-of-bounds data are still valid but push zero-padded values during execution.

implicit_assumptions.description: Pre-computing valid jump destinations prevents attackers from jumping into PUSH data to execute arbitrary byte sequences as opcodes.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Arbitrary code execution within contracts, potentially bypassing security checks or accessing unauthorized functionality.

implicit_assumptions.description: Jump destination analysis is performed once per contract call and cached for the duration of execution.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Re-computing on every JUMP would cause significant performance overhead, potentially enabling gas-based DoS attacks.

implicit_assumptions.description: The JUMPDEST opcode (0x5B) is reserved and cannot appear naturally in contract execution except as a valid jump target.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: If 0x5B could be interpreted differently in certain contexts, jump validation could be bypassed.

implicit_assumptions.description: Contract bytecode is immutable after deployment, so valid jump destinations cannot change.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Mutable bytecode would require re-analysis of jump destinations, introducing security and performance concerns.
